Create a rough stacked bar chart

Source: R/roughViz.R
roughStackedBar.Rd

Displays stacked columns suitable for showing parts-of-a-whole across categories.

Usage

roughStackedBar(
  data,
  labels = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  colors = NULL,
  roughness = 1,
  fillStyle = "hachure",
  fillWeight = NULL,
  strokeWidth = 1,
  bowing = 0,
  simplification = 0.2,
  font = 0,
  margin = NULL,
  axisFontSize = "1rem",
  axisRoughness = 0.5,
  axisStrokeWidth = 0.5,
  innerStrokeWidth = 0,
  padding = 0.1,
  titleAlign = "center",
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A `data.frame` or named list. With a data frame one column should contain the category labels while the remaining numeric columns represent the individual stacks.

labels

Column name that holds the category labels when `data` is a data frame.

title

Optional heading.

width

Optional width of the widget (numeric pixels or CSS units).

height

Optional height of the widget (numeric pixels or CSS units).

colors

Character vector of fill colours recycled across the stacks.

roughness

Roughness level forwarded to roughViz.js.

fillStyle

Fill style for the stack segments.

fillWeight

Thickness of the fill pattern strokes.

strokeWidth

Outline stroke width.

bowing

Amount of curvature applied to straight segments.

simplification

Simplification tolerance for shapes.

font

Font family reference (`0`, `1`, or custom name).

margin

Named list of margins around the plot.

axisFontSize

Font size used for axis labels (CSS units or numbers).

axisRoughness

Roughness setting applied to axes.

axisStrokeWidth

Axis line stroke width.

innerStrokeWidth

Stroke width drawn inside the stacked bars.

padding

Gap between categories (0-1 range).

titleAlign

Horizontal alignment of the title (`"left"`, `"center"`, or `"right"`).

...

Additional named options forwarded to roughViz.js.

Value

A stacked bar `htmlwidget`.

Details

When `data` is a data frame the function verifies the presence of `labels` and at least one additional numeric column. It then coerces those numeric columns to double precision before handing the data to roughViz.js.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  revenue <- data.frame(
    quarter = c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"),
    hardware = c(5, 6, 4, 7),
    software = c(3, 4, 6, 5),
    services = c(2, 3, 2, 4)
  )

  roughStackedBar(
    data = revenue,
    labels = "quarter",
    title = "Product mix by quarter",
    colors = c("#90be6d", "#f9c74f", "#f94144")
  )
}
